lyrics:
[Intro: solo piano, simple rocking figure]

[Verse 1: soft, plain, piano only]
Suppose there was a table
As long as any road
And nobody went hungry
And nobody was owed

[Verse 2: soft strings enter]
Suppose the maps were pencil
And the borders rubbed away
Suppose we all woke early
With nothing to repay

[Chorus: voice lifts, bass and light drums]
I know how it sounds, believe me
I have heard it since I was ten
But somebody has to say it
Or we never start, and then
Suppose we did

[Verse 3: soft, strings fuller]
Suppose the news was weather
And the weather wasn't war
Suppose we knew our neighbours' names
And what they're hoping for

[Chorus: voice lifts, bass and light drums]
I know how it sounds, believe me
I have heard it since I was ten
But somebody has to say it
Or we never start, and then
Suppose we did

[Outro: piano alone, last line nearly spoken]
Pull up a chair
Suppose we did
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 76 BPM, 4/4, C major. Slow, simple and still. A lullaby for adults.

VOICE: Male tenor, soft, plain and slightly nasal, with a touch of echo on it. He sings quietly and without drama, almost as if thinking aloud. A small lift in the chorus, nothing more. The last line is nearly spoken.

INSTRUMENTS: An upright-sounding piano playing a gentle, rocking chord figure with a small decorative turn. A soft string section. A simple, quiet bass. Very light drums with a soft backbeat. Nothing else.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano. 0:13 Verse 1. 0:38 Verse 2, strings. 1:03 Chorus 1, bass and drums. 1:32 Verse 3. 1:57 Chorus 2. 2:26 Outro, piano alone and two quiet lines, ending at 3:05.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-1970s home-studio simplicity: warm, a little soft-edged, piano and voice close with a short echo, strings distant.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The piano figure in the first four seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original asks us to imagine things gone. This asks us to try things: a table, pencilled maps, knowing a neighbour's name. The last line is an invitation to sit down, which is how change looks to someone who has run a few meetings.

EMOTIONAL ARC: A quiet proposal, a shrug at the doubters, an invitation.
